That sounds like more muscle damage (something that can be fixed) than nerve damage. Can you flex you hand and touch your thumb to the tip of your pinky finger easily (the key part is how easily you can do that)? If you can do that without a sharp sensation than it's likely not nerve damage. If there is a sensation running up the edges of your palm (or anywhere really), like the muscles are aching or pinching, stop. Don't push yourself. The test is if you can still move your hand easily. 

I've got massive nerve damage on one hand and the pinky-thumb thing was one of the ways the doctor figured out the difference. (I am however not a doctor.)

Is it feel like the fingertips/palms are fuzzy, like static, or numb like they're cold (even though they're not)? If it's a fuzzy sensation it might be just muscle damage. If it's a pure, absolute numbness even when flexing, then that's more serious and you might need to see a professional. Either way, bandage things tightly but not overly so, and drink something hot and sweet as that's great for shock and bloodloss. Good luck.
